title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the cote is Grothendieck's material on the Galois theory of motives. This handwritten page sits between typed pages on holomorphic ODEs, which are unrelated. The page works out a concrete arithmetic example, apparently the 'supersingular' motive over F_p.

The setting. Let xi in Br(Q) be the class of the quaternion algebra D ramified exactly at p and infinity; the transcription says '2 et infini', but the later use of p strongly suggests p. D is the endomorphism algebra (up to isogeny) of supersingular elliptic curves over F_p-bar. Let O be a maximal order. Let C be the associated Z-linear category, essentially right O-modules via the Deuring correspondence: supersingular curves correspond to left/right ideal classes of O. Let T be some additional structure, most plausibly a norm or fibre-functor datum.

The object Bord(C). Grothendieck considers Bord(C), a strictly commutative Picard category, best read as the Picard category of autoequivalences (invertible O-bimodules) of C. He finds it is split ('déployée'), with invariants pi_0 = Z/2 and pi_1 = Z/2:
- pi_1 = units of the centre, Z^* = {±1}.
- pi_0 = group of two-sided ideal classes of O, generated by the unique prime m above p, with m^2 = pO.
- The generator rho of pi_0 is the Frobenius-twist functor E -> E^(p) = E/Ker F_E. This is the classical Deuring correspondence between the Frobenius isogeny and the two-sided prime m.

The norm and the lift. The reduced norm sends m to N(m) = pZ inside N(O) = Z. Choosing the generator p of pZ gives a lift rho-bar = p. The pair (rho, rho-bar) is then an object of Bord(C,T), the Picard category of pairs (autoequivalence, trivialisation of its norm).

Base changes.
- If p is invertible in A': Bord(C_A', T_A') is identified with H^1(S', mu_2), with S' = Spec A'. The image of (rho, rho-bar) is the class of p modulo squares, via the Kummer sequence.
- If A' = Z_p: Bord(C'_p, T'_p) is an extension of Z/2 (from pi_0, generated by m) by Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2}, which is Z/2 for p ≠ 2 and corresponds to H^1(Z_p, mu_2). It sits inside Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} x Z/2 and is generated by (m, p).
- The isomorphism classes of the data then form a torsor under a group C, which is (Z/2)^2 for p ≠ 2.
- If A' = R: take the gerbe G over Z[1/p] defined by C (the mu_2- or G_m-gerbe of the Azumaya algebra D ⊗ Z[1/p]) and its restriction G_R. The equivalences of G_R with the 'type' gerbe over R (its 'polarisations') form a torsor under H^1(R, mu_2) = R^*/R^{*2}.

Purpose. The page prepares a local-global count (Z[1/p], Z_p, R) of the forms or rigidifications of a non-neutral integral Tannakian-type structure. That structure is attached to supersingular elliptic curves, the standard example showing that motives over F_p admit no Q-valued fibre functor.
errors: Ramification is transcribed as 'en 2 et infini'. The rest of the page (unique prime m over p, Frobenius over F_p, N(m) = pZ) requires ramification at p and infinity, so this is either a misreading or a slip.

The meaning of 'Bord' and of the auxiliary structure T is not defined on this page, so the identification of Bord(C_A', T_A') with H^1(S', mu_2) cannot be fully checked. It is consistent if T is a trivialisation of the reduced norm: the automorphisms of the unit then give mu_2, and the pi_0 part is killed once p is a unit.
Over Z_p for p = 2, Z_2^*/Z_2^{*2} is (Z/2)^2, not Z/2. Grothendieck correctly flags the p ≠ 2 restriction.

ideas.what: Picard category of autoequivalences of the category attached to a maximal order in the definite quaternion algebra ramified at p and infinity; pi_0 = Z/2 generated by the two-sided prime over p, pi_1 = {±1}
ideas.modern_name: Picard group / Picard 2-group of an Azumaya algebra or maximal order (two-sided ideal class group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (ideals), Fröhlich, Bass ('Picard groups of noncommutative rings', ~1970s)

ideas.what: Frobenius twist E -> E^(p) corresponds to the unique two-sided prime m of O over p
ideas.modern_name: Deuring correspondence / Frobenius as the ideal of norm p

ideas.what: Rigidifying via the reduced norm (rho-bar = p) and computing the resulting Picard category over Z[1/p], Z_p and R as H^1(-, mu_2)-torsors and extensions
ideas.modern_name: Integral/local forms of non-neutral Tannakian categories; gerbes with band mu_2 attached to Azumaya algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (gerbes, 1971), Saavedra Rivano (Tannakian categories, 1972), Milne (motives over finite fields)

ideas.what: Supersingular elliptic curves giving a quaternionic, non-neutral motivic structure, treated integrally rather than over Q
ideas.modern_name: Motivic gerbe over F_p; supersingular motive

missed.claim: Grothendieck computes, integrally over Z, Z[1/p], Z_p and R, the Picard category of autoequivalences of the (C,T) attached to the supersingular quaternion order, apparently aiming at a local-global classification of integral forms of the motivic gerbe. The literature on motivic gerbes over finite fields (Langlands–Rapoport, Milne) works rationally, not with Z-integral structures and their Picard 2-groups.
missed.quote: Bord(C) est la catégorie de Picard déployée d'invariants Z/2Z, Z/2Z ... Bord(C_{A'},T_{A'}) = H^1(S',mu_2) ... l'image de (rho, rho-bar) ... la classe de p modulo les carrés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early example of an integral (over Z) Tannakian/gerbe-theoretic treatment of supersingular motives, including mu_2 'polarisation' torsors at R and Z_p. It is of possible interest for integral motivic Galois groups, but the content is mostly classical quaternion-order arithmetic.

deep.surprise_reason: It is an interesting 1965-era integral computation linking a Picard-category / gerbe formalism to the Deuring quaternion order and the Frobenius twist. The individual facts are classical, and the framework (the meaning of Bord, T) is too fragmentary on this page to constitute a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'ramifié seulement en 2 et ∞' is very probably 'ramifié seulement en p et ∞'.
'le générateur rho de pi_0 ligne[?]' should probably read 'le générateur rho de pi_0 (lequel correspond au foncteur ...'.
'H^1(Z_p, mu_2)' is written beneath Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} as an identification.
'gerbe de liens[?]' is likely 'gerbe de liens mu_2' or simply 'la gerbe'; '(= ensemble des polarisations de la gerbe)' looks right.
Margin 'C_p = C', T_p = T'' gives notation for the Z_p base change.
